'''Petr Cornelie''' (born July 26, 1995) is a French professional basketball player. He stands 210 cm (6'11'’) tall and plays both the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and the [[Center (basketball)|center]] spots. Cornelie is currently under contract with [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket]] of the French [[LNB Pro A|Pro A]] league.

== Career ==
Growing up in [[Alsace]], Cornelie played in the youth ranks of Saint-Joseph Strasbourg, Basket Club Souffelweyersheim and Association sportive d'Electricité de Strasbourg.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dna.fr/sports/2015/06/01/cornelie-l-alsacien|title=Cornelie, l'Alsacien|website=www.dna.fr|access-date=2016-03-27}}</ref>

At the age of 15, he joined the youth academy of [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.letelegramme.fr/omnisports/cornelie-la-nouvelle-pepite-du-mans-06-09-2015-10763652.php|title=Cornelie, la nouvelle pépite du Mans|website=Le Telegramme|access-date=2016-03-27}}</ref> He made his debut on Le Mans' men's team during the 2013–14 season and became a regular on the team the following season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Pro-A/200006/Joueurs/A55324/Cornelie-Petr|title=Petr Cornelie – Le Mans – Joueurs – Pro A – LNB.fr|website=www.lnb.fr|access-date=2016-03-27}}</ref> In the 2014–15 season he won the Pro A Rising Star award.

On June 13, 2016, Cornelie was one of 13 different international underclassmen (including one of four other Frenchmen) to enter their names for the [[2016 NBA Draft]]. Cornelie is projected to be a late first round or early second round selection in this year's draft.

== International career ==
Cornelie played for France at the 2012 U17 World Championships in Lithuania,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://kaunas2012.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/12/fu17wc/men/player/p/eid/6228/pid/93515/rid//sid/6228/tid/282/profile.html|title=Petr Cornelie profile, FIBA U17 World Championship for Men 2012 {{!}} FIBA.COM|website=FIBA.COM|access-date=2016-03-27}}</ref> at the 2013 U18 European Championships in Latvia<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.season_2013.roundID_9420.teamID_282.playerID_93515.html|title=Petr Cornelie {{!}} U18 European Championship Men (2013) {{!}} FIBA Europe|website=www.fibaeurope.com|access-date=2016-03-27}}</ref> and at the 2015 U20 European Championships in Italy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/93515/sid/11585/tid/282/_/2015_U20_European_Championship_Men/index.html|title=Petr Cornelie profile, U20 European Championship Men 2015 {{!}} FIBA.COM|website=FIBA.COM|access-date=2016-03-27}}</ref>

== Personal info ==
His mother Pavla Sigmundova is a former Czech basketball player, his father Martial Cornelie played basketball in the Pro B, the second-tier of French basketball.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Accueil/100003/Article/25656/Petr-Cornelie-le-futur-en-grand|title=Petr Cornelie, le futur en grand|website=www.lnb.fr|access-date=2016-03-27}}</ref> Petr's sister Jodie Cornelie-Sigmundova played internationally for the French junior national teams and spent four years on the University of Dayton Flyers women's basketball team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://daytonflyers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2498|title=Jodie Cornelie-Sigmundova – 2015–16 Women's Basketball|access-date=2016-03-27}}</ref>
